correctness.rationale: The strict coefficient bounds control deviations of each edge factor from +1 or −1 over the entire edge, giving a counterclockwise boundary with no intervening equilibria. The corner rates follow from the diagonal entries −2xP and −2yQ at x,y=±1, where P,Q are the printed quadratic factors. Multiplying the four stable-to-unstable rates gives (1). Integrating the logarithmic rates in shrinking saddle boxes gives each saddle passage exponent; regular transitions from fixed sections to smaller boxes and along open edges have nonzero finite derivatives, hence exponent 1. Composition gives the logarithmic exponent, not an exact monomial return map. On the slice the denominator stays positive and the sign is the sign of 4h²(1+ε)²−8ε(1+ε²). The finding's iff phrasing is valid only off equality, as explicitly scoped by the repeated exclusion of ρ=1; it cannot establish nonattraction or nonrepulsion at equality. The focus has eigenvalues −ε±i and the formal second root is strictly below x=−1. The attracting collar excludes the focus basin closure from the boundary, so its interior basin boundary is a nonempty compact invariant set with no rest point. Poincaré–Bendixson gives an interior periodic orbit, without claiming uniqueness, hyperbolicity or stability. The witness gives ρ=32019867/26185967 and second root −10001/2525; no witness was inferred from the finite mesh, and the uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: An explicit interior-cycle region would be useful if it required new analysis of this family. Here the exact product is already available for arbitrary polynomial corner factors; the proposed chamber and two-parameter slice just make its substitution simple, and the existence proof supplies a standard planar consequence of the resulting trappings.
